title: SproutLink vs. Linktree: Which link-in-bio tool is right for your brand?
content:
Your viral Reels and engaging carousel posts attract audiences on Instagram. But what happens when you want to get this audience to visit your website? Whether you want them to read a new post, check out your new collection or sign up for an event, you need a seamless link-in-bio strategy to drive traffic from Instagram to your site.
With Instagram limiting clickable caption links exclusively to Meta One subscribers, your bio link serves as prime real estate. Even then, you have only five spots to add your URLs. That means constantly swapping links every time you post something with a different landing page.
Link-in-bio tools like SproutLink and Linktree save you the trouble with dynamic landing pages that lead to multiple destinations.
Which tool should you use? While Linktree pioneered the link-in-bio category, SproutLink integrates directly into your publishing workflow. This post compares the two options, so you can decide on the right fit for your brand.
SproutLink is Sprout Social’s proprietary and customizable link-in-bio solution that turns your social traffic into website visits, leads and revenue. Designed for use across multiple platforms—including Instagram, TikTok and other major social networks—SproutLink allows you to create a branded, centralized landing page featuring custom call-to-action buttons, direct social profile links and an optional clickable replica of your Instagram grid.
Because SproutLink lives directly within the publishing workflow, you can attach destination URLs while scheduling new posts in Compose or add links to existing posts retroactively—streamlining your publishing and link management in one centralized place.
Linktree is a standalone link-in-bio tool that hosts all your URLs in a simple, list-style landing page. It supports broad, platform-agnostic use, letting you centralize link management across all your social media profiles, not just Instagram.
Available in free and paid tiers, Linktree offers ready-made templates and a straightforward interface that makes it a beginner-friendly option.
Both SproutLink and Linktree offer the essentials to manage your bio links in one place. The key difference is that SproutLink is a feature integrated within a comprehensive social media management ecosystem, while Linktree is a dedicated link-in-bio tool that also features a built-in Social Planner for content scheduling.
This distinction drives the main differences in workflow and pricing.
SproutLink costs more because it’s part of a full social media management platform. This also means it comes with powerful tools to manage every aspect of your social media, including publishing and reporting. The feature integrates directly with the rest of your publishing workflow, meaning you can attach links while composing a new post in Sprout.
Meanwhile, Linktree is a popular tool for managing social media bio links and scheduling posts. It costs less to get started and comes with a free plan for basic links. It’s platform-agnostic, meaning you can use it to manage links in bio for Facebook and TikTok, not just Instagram.
Linktree also features a built-in Social Planner on paid plans that allows you to schedule and auto-post content across your social platforms. You can even schedule links and posts to go live at the same time, giving you a hands-free workflow.
Ultimately, deciding between the two comes down to your specific use case.
The comparison chart above gives you a better sense of what each tool offers, but how do they measure up in actual performance? Here’s what real users have to say on different review sites:
Although Sprout scores slightly lower than Linktree, review volume reveals a significant difference. This volume gap highlights a difference in scope, not just sentiment. G2 reviewers are rating the whole Sprout suite instead of just the link-in-bio feature.
This data reinforces that G2 reviewers are rating the whole Sprout suite , used across company sizes, rather than just a small-business tool.
*The comparison data in this article is based on G2 data from 10/21/2026, unless stated otherwise.
Linktree slightly outranks Sprout even on Capterra , but the gap in review volume is evident. User satisfaction scores for Sprout Social reflect ratings for a wide range of social media management features, not just limited to links in bio.
Note: Linktree’s high “ease of use” score (4.6**) reflects doing one thing well, while Sprout Social’s rating (4.4**) reflects an entire platform’s worth of functionality that includes SproutLink.
**The comparison data in this article is based on Capterra data from 10/21/2026, unless stated otherwise.
While SproutLink holds up as a strong Linktree alternative, it’s no longer about which tool has better reviews. Instead, you need to think about whether you need a link-in-bio tool or a platform that includes one.
Sprout Social combines your link-in-bio management with every other aspect of your social media. That means you don’t just get Instagram link-in-bio features. You also get scheduling, publishing and reporting all in one place.
This saves you the trouble of stitching together a link tool with a separate scheduler and manually adding a new link to your custom landing page every time.
Choosing a full social media management platform doesn’t have to cost hundreds of dollars each month. With low-cost starter options like the Sprout Essentials plan , you get access to SproutLink along with all the basic publishing, scheduling and reporting features. Starting at $79 per seat per month, the plan lets you:
This makes it a solid choice for brands outgrowing manual posting that need their bio link connected to a broader content and reporting workflow.
“Sprout Social is clearly designed with Social Media Managers in mind,” states Alyssa R. , a social media manager for a mid-market non-profit organization.
“As a one-person social team, I need to maximize my productivity, and I rely on Sprout every day. Its features, such as SproutLink in bio, the ability to toggle a single post across multiple platforms and the AI Alt Text Generator, have helped me streamline my workflow.”
Linktree is a link management tool that offers basic publishing and analytics features. SproutLink is a feature of a larger, more robust social media management platform. Both tools offer unique value depending on your needs.
With this in mind, here’s a quick guideline to help you make the right choice.
As the tool that pioneered bio links, Linktree continues to dominate the link-in-bio landscape. But with alternatives like SproutLink that integrate with your publishing workflow, management becomes effortless without the need to constantly switch platforms.
The choice comes down to whether you need a standalone tool or a comprehensive platform to manage your entire social strategy, bio links included.
Still not sure if SproutLink is the right choice for you? Start your free trial of Sprout Essentials and get SproutLink, scheduling and reporting in one place.
Disclaimer: The comparison data in this article is based on G2 and Capterra data from 10/21/2026, unless stated otherwise. Pricing, features and ratings are accurate as of that date and may have changed.
SproutLink is not free, but it’s included with every Sprout Social plan, which starts at $79 per month.
Does SproutLink work on platforms other than Instagram?
No, SproutLink only works for Instagram profiles at this time.
Yes, you can switch from Linktree to SproutLink when you sign up for any of the Sprout Social plans.
Do I need a specific Sprout Social plan to use SproutLink?
No, you don’t need a specific Sprout Social plan to use SproutLink. The feature is available across every plan level.
SproutLink tracks clicks by monitoring user engagement on your custom SproutLink landing page. It attributes link clicks to specific posts, tracks post clicks and daily page views and updates metrics every hour.

title: How to create a Black Friday social media marketing strategy
content:
Black Friday prep is happening earlier than ever for shoppers this year. Your customers are already looking for deals online and increasingly on social media . According to a Q3 2026 Sprout Social Pulse Survey, 78% of users plan to use social as much or more than they did last year to help them find and purchase gifts this year.
Social media is now tied with physical stores for gift purchase discovery, with 46% of customers marking them as top choices. As customers face increasing economic pressure this year, many are using social media to research the best deals. If you want to make the most of Black Friday on social media, start planning your strategy now. Customers are eager for ideas well before November.
In this guide, we walk through how to build effective Black Friday social media campaigns this Q4.
Spurred by the growth of online shopping and social commerce , Black Friday has become a multi-day event, including Small Business Saturday and Cyber Monday. According to the data, customers are thinking about their holiday shopping differently this year, and ecommerce is a key part of their plans.
More than half of respondents (69%) to the Q3 2026 pulse survey said they’re concerned about rising prices due to tariffs. Over a third (36%) are planning to shop earlier to specifically avoid tariff-related price jumps, and 56% are planning to reduce their holiday spending overall due to economic conditions.
For brands, that means competition is higher and earning customer trust will take more legwork. To create a winning Black Friday marketing strategy, it’s crucial to tap into the power of social.
Nearly a quarter (23%) of the Q3 pulse survey respondents said the quality of a company’s social media customer service makes them more likely to purchase this holiday season, and a similar percentage said the originality of holiday-specific social content makes a difference. Here are different types of Black Friday social media posts that have worked for other brands to inspire your campaign planning.
Partner with influencers to create tailored content for specific demographics. From fashion lovers to tech enthusiasts, influencers can connect with high-intent niche audiences . If your Black Friday deals are perfect for a particular type of customer, working with influencers who already speak to that crowd can build trust and revenue
Offering special discounts and promo codes via influencers is one way to track ROI of a campaign and boost sales. In fact, promo codes are the leading factor influencing the purchasing decisions of social media scrollers. Thirty percent of respondents to the Q3 pulse survey said promo codes influencers share make them more likely to purchase from a brand during the holidays, more than any other factor in the survey.
Keep in mind that follower count is not the main barometer of impact for your influencer partnerships. Instead, focus on social media discoverability. Working with influencers who can create hyper-relevant content is key to getting your campaign seen by new audiences. Small businesses with modest budgets and larger companies alike can embrace micro-influencer marketing this gifting season.
For example, Rilee Smith, a travel and packing influencer on Instagram, crafted a video in partnership with five of her favorite bag brands to offer her followers a slate of Black Friday sales. Her video showed each of the bags in action and what discounts the brands offered.
Grab consumer attention by giving away free merchandise. Create a social media giveaway or contest to improve your engagement and supercharge the buzz around your brand.
Giveaways and contests boost your follower count, convert leads, amplify brand awareness and increase loyalty.
You can tie giveaways to an influencer campaign or a specific product. Supplement brand Blume held a Black Friday giveaway featuring their SuperBelly product line. The giveaway post also mentioned their Black Friday sale and required specific engagements to enter. The result was promotion of the giveaway and the broader discounts available for the shopping-centric weekend.
Want to incentivize your audience to return to your website or shop with you after Black Friday ends? Promote your rewards or loyalty program. These programs typically offer discounts, coupons or early access to repeat shoppers—all of which encourage brand loyalty .
The cost savings loyalty programs offer are especially appealing to customers this year and create a way to build trust with your audience. Discounts, special social content and exclusive savings for your loyalty members show them you know their discretionary dollars are valuable, and you’re willing to go the extra mile to keep them coming back.
Luggage brand SWISSGEAR offered their rewards members early access to a 60% off Black Friday sale. Customers looking to plan their holiday purchases as early as possible this year will appreciate a first shot at discounts and bundles. Your social channels are a useful tool alongside email marketing to let members know about exclusive benefits for the holidays.
When consumers shop on social, they don’t stick to a single platform. They’re browsing TikTok, Instagram, Reddit, Pinterest and more. Their research does include traditional marketing avenues like print, digital and brick and mortar stores, too. Our Q3 pulse survey found that shoppers are sourcing gift ideas from a variety of sources:
Due to social media saturation , it’s important for brands to take a multichannel marketing approach to reach audiences and break through the noise. This includes all of your social channels, digital touchpoints and even real life activations.
During Black Friday, use omnichannel marketing by creating a seamless customer experience, from your social networks and chatbots to email strategy and customer care. UK brand Gymshark’s annual Blackout event on Black Friday incorporates several of their social media channels, their physical stores, email and Reddit posts.
A brand community comprises people who have an emotional connection to your brand. When you reach your community effectively, you increase brand loyalty and even encourage customers to become brand evangelists.
Take a cue from your community when creating your Black Friday content. Get to know their other favorite brands, personal values and how they spend their holidays. Use these insights to guide your social content development. Look for ways to give back to causes your audience cares about, and that align to your brand values.
On GivingTuesday —the Tuesday after Black Friday when people make donations to charitable organizations—Ulta Beauty shared about two partnerships it participated in for the occasion. This included a special product bundle customers could purchase to support the cause.
When developing a Black Friday social media marketing strategy, you need to plan ahead. Now is the time to get your content calendar in order, take stock of what’s been successful for you this year (metrics-wise) and think about how you will stand out in a swarm of other Black Friday social media campaigns.
Follow these tips to execute your Black Friday social-first marketing strategy successfully.
Build awareness for your brand by engaging new potential followers and email subscribers. Use an early-bird special to entice customers to follow your social accounts or to opt-in to your email newsletter for a unique Black Friday discount code.
Focus on growing your customer base before Black Friday so your content can reach a wider audience.
Kick off your Black Friday campaigns early to A/B test your different creative options. For example, analyze how a short-form video performs compared to a static graphic with the same message.
As Black Friday approaches, go with the creative format that will bring the most engagement, awareness and positive sentiment.
Using a data-driven approach to guide your Black Friday marketing can help you yield better results (e.g. more engagements and conversions) by ensuring you use the creative that most resonates with your audience.
Creators and influencers can help you generate more engagement, reach new audiences and strengthen your community on social this Black Friday. Search for creators that are topically relevant to your campaign, and start reaching out to them as soon as possible to build the most impactful campaigns.
Finding and vetting these creators is easier with Sprout Social Influencer Marketing. Our AI-powered semantic search capabilities take a closer look at the context of influencer content, making it easier to assess influencers’ alignment with your brand and audience.
For example, say you work in the travel industry and want to partner with influencers to promote your Black Friday holiday package deals. Rather than manually hunting for creators with a travel niche, you can simply search “Europe travel vlog” or “budget travel tips”.
Sprout Social Influencer Marketing will then show creators who explore relevant themes and topics in their content, even if those phrases don’t appear verbatim. This makes it easier to find a broader range of influencers, including those you might’ve overlooked with standard search filters.
For your Black Friday promotions, keep in mind that consumers prefer content from influencers who have used your products before. The 2026 Influencer Marketing Report found that 37% say the influencer should have used the product at least once, and 44% say the influencer should have been using the product for a long time. The holiday season is a great time to tap existing brand partnerships and work with influencers who have had successful campaigns for you in the past.
Align your Black Friday influencer content with what your audience cares most about to drive engagement and foster trust. Look to campaigns that have done well in the past for ideas.
One of the easiest ways to prepare for Black Friday is to get your profiles ready. An up-to-date profile is essential to converting viewers and followers into buyers and brand superfans.
People will first notice your profile photos (both headers and profile pics). Consider updating your pictures with a holiday-inspired or sale-focused theme.
Consider also adding links in your profile bios (Instagram, X, TikTok) or About sections (Facebook, LinkedIn) to your Black Friday promos.
Refreshing visuals and links across your social media profiles can help grab user attention and entice them to click—essential for increasing Black Friday sales.
Expect to ramp up your customer care strategy and content production as you enter the holiday season. Customer care is particularly important. While it may be one of the busiest times of year, it can’t fall to the wayside—if it does, you might lose your customers. According to the Q3 pulse survey, 27% of consumers plan to use social media more this year for holiday customer service needs, and 38% expect a response from brands within 1-2 hours.
Here’s how you can use  a social media management platform like Sprout to level up your holiday customer service :
You can also use Sprout’s automation and AI marketing resources to manage other elements of your social media strategy, scale smoothly and prevent burnout:
These tools will help you seamlessly and effectively execute in advance and during the big sale.
With the help of automations and AI, social media management tools empower your team to provide quick and personalized customer care, optimize content development and build stronger social strategies.
If you serve one specific, hyper-niche audience, skip to the next section. But, if you have several audience types, you should create different Black Friday social media posts for each market segment.
For example, department stores should create posts highlighting holiday deals geared toward different audiences, whether it’s a customer interested in home decor and electronics or looking for clothing and outdoor gear.
Tailor your Black Friday marketing to your audience segments (including their interests and product preferences) to enhance relevance and, in turn, drive engagement.
Creating a reporting strategy for your Black Friday campaign is key to knowing what worked and what needs tweaking. A campaign performance report should provide insights on reach, engagement and conversions to see if your marketing efforts hit the mark. Sprout’s Trellis features a Performance and Engagement agent that helps you extract those metrics from across your social media accounts. This saves you the busy work and aggregates insights quickly so you can pivot as needed during the holiday season.
Having these insights at hand will also help you make smarter, data-driven decisions to optimize your budget and resources for next year.
It’s never too early to start planning future Black Friday campaigns. Draw insights from this year’s campaign data to refine your strategy, allocate resources more effectively and yield greater results in years to come.
Take a look at these successful Black Friday social media campaigns to help get the ball rolling as you plan yours.
Glossier’s marketing approach leans into real, everyday people using their products. While their social feed is full of aesthetically pleasing photos, the content is also approachable and achievable.
For Black Friday, Glossier kept that same tone and recruited a number of employees to share what items they were getting for themselves and for gifting during Black Friday sales.
The brand shared a carousel of recommendations from team members placed over photos of the products themselves. It was a riff on the typical influencer strategy, turning employees who live and breathe the products into valuable word-of-mouth promo. And with 40% of all consumers frequently (once a month or more) discovering a product or service through employee-generated content, it’s a strategy that will inevitably drive sales.
More than ever, customers are looking for the humans behind the brand that they can relate to. For Black Friday deals, your team can provide approachable, likable voices without the lift of a full influencer partnership.
Black Friday in the pre-social media era was built around “doorbuster” deals that had people lining up outside right after Thanksgiving dinner. Lowe’s leveraged nostalgia for the Black Friday of yesterday, popular unboxing videos and strategic scarcity to drive a surge in interest to their stores.
The Lowe’s Black Friday Bucket Giveaway tied together a giveaway, benefits for loyalty members and the power of UGC content in one campaign. The first 50 Lowe’s Rewards members in line at their retail locations on Black Friday received a blue bucket filled with branded products. Each bucket had a chance to win $2,000 toward an appliance purchase.
The social promo featured a blurred look at products in the bucket to heighten the mystery. As customers received their buckets on Black Friday, UGC posts flooded in. Customers eagerly recorded their bucket “unboxings” and a lucky few posted the thrill of being the $2,000 winners. A fairly humble item—a blue bucket—turned into a boon for those who received free appliances and the Lowe’s brand overall.
GoPro has built a thriving community around their cameras. GoPro loyalists actively debate different cameras, share tips for getting the best shots and trade ideas across channels. A major chunk of the brand’s social media content comes from community submitted photos and videos for the GoPro Awards or shared on users’ personal pages.
While many of the videos shared are breathtaking, featuring extreme sports and beautiful locales, some capture the lighter side of life and the GoPro brand humour. For Black Friday, GoPro shared a series of posts of community content with a dash of silliness.
From an up close and personal shot of a cute dog’s snout to a Redbull athlete “collecting coins” on a bike to add up to the Black Friday discount, these posts offer entertainment and connection via community-created content. And keep the brand grounded in their customers’ literal and metaphorical viewpoint.
To prepare for the retail holiday, make sure your Black Friday social media campaign and customer care strategy are in place well before the end of November. Keep in mind consumers’ economic mindset this year as you develop your approach, and look for ways to meet their needs, and offer a bit of delight while doing so. Social media users are stretching their dollars this year, and each purchase feels like a bigger decision.
Your Black Friday social media campaigns should go beyond offering a one-time deal and instead open the door for ongoing brand connection. As you build your campaign, remember to reinforce your mission, align with your organization’s goals, make your creative count and schedule your content ahead of time.
